text.arabic_uthmani: فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُمْ ۘ يَوْمَ يَدْعُ ٱلدَّاعِ إِلَىٰ شَىْءٍۢ نُّكُرٍ

words.gloss_range: opening connective particle; locally marks a consequence and resumption into direct command

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: neighboring imperative named by the opening particle

words.prose: {{ar:فَ}} ({{tr:fa-}}) makes the ayah begin as a consequence, not as a clean reset. It resumes the discourse after the failed warnings and immediately turns that failure into the premise for the command that follows. Because the particle is fused onto {{ar:تَوَلَّ}} ({{tr:tawalla}}), the boundary logic and the withdrawal command arrive in one compressed opening beat. The shift from prior third-person description into direct address is therefore already underway before the verb is fully heard.

topics.headline: consequence and resumption before the command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command is grammatically presented as the next consequence of failed warning, not as an unrelated new instruction.
topics.reason: The particle is licensed as the opening connective, and the CRITICAL rows coherently preserve both resumption and causal consequence.

topics.headline: proclitic fusion compresses the opening beat
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not first state a connector and then a command; the fused surface makes consequence and command land together.
topics.reason: The surface particle is proclitic to the following imperative, so the form-level rows survive as a compact opening-beat payoff.

topics.headline: prior narration becomes second-person command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the address mode turning from the deniers being described to the Prophet being commanded.
topics.reason: The following verb carries second-person masculine singular imperative force, so the transition row is locally supported.

words.gloss_range: Form V second-person masculine singular command to turn away; locally selected by the following away-from complement
words.root_gloss_range: broad root field of nearness, authority, alliance, turning, and separation; local Form V with the away-from complement selects managed withdrawal while leaving relational pressure audible

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following away-from complement that selects withdrawal
following temporal frame adjacent to the command

words.prose: {{ar:تَوَلَّ}} ({{tr:tawalla}}) is a direct second-person command, not a report that someone turned away. The Form V shape makes the addressee take up the distancing himself, and the following {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}) selects withdrawal rather than the root family's taking-charge or alliance branches. That matters because {{ar:و ل ي}} ({{tr:w-l-y}}) often carries nearness, authority, or affiliation pressure; here that relation is actively reversed into disengagement from the known group. The command also stands before the Day-scene, so prophetic disengagement becomes the human-facing entry point before the caller summons toward the unnamed destination. The formulaic comparison with other turn-away commands (6:68, 43:89, 53:29) supports the disengagement frame, while the local syntax keeps this instance tied to the summons that follows.

topics.headline: nearness and authority reversed by the away-from complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the root field of nearness or charge is not erased; the away-from complement turns that relational field into commanded disengagement.
topics.reason: The following complement forces the withdrawal branch, so broader governance and alliance senses survive only as contrastive root pressure.

topics.headline: self-directed singular command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command is singular, direct, and self-enacted rather than a general policy statement.
topics.reason: The verb form and attachment support identify a second-person masculine singular imperative with an implicit addressee.

topics.headline: command before the eschatological summons
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah moves from a command to withdraw from them into another call that draws toward a destination.
topics.reason: The local sequence places the imperative before the temporal calling scene, and the CRITICAL rows preserve a real discourse pivot.

topics.headline: temporal entanglement with the following Day frame
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the command is not isolated from the Day-frame, even though the strongest local attachment takes the time phrase forward with the calling scene.
topics.reason: The row overstates possible government by the command; attachment evidence makes {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) the temporal frame for the calling, while the command remains structurally adjacent to that frame.

words.gloss_range: away-from preposition plus third-person masculine plural suffix; locally the required complement naming the source group of withdrawal

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: governing imperative completed by this complement
final destination phrase used for directional contrast

words.prose: {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}) completes the command by naming the source from whom withdrawal occurs. The phrase is not an optional afterthought: the preposition supplies the required away-from relation for {{ar:تَوَلَّ}} ({{tr:tawalla}}), and the suffix makes the target a known prior group. The command therefore closes around the earlier deniers before the ayah opens the Day-scene. Its direction also prepares the later opposite movement: away from them here, then toward {{ar:شَىْءٍ نُّكُرٍ}} ({{tr:shayʾin nukurin}}) at the end.

topics.headline: required away-from complement
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that withdrawal has a governed source; without this phrase the verb could be misread as open-ended or even as another root branch.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces the phrase as the complement of the command and selects separation over aboutness or substitution.

topics.headline: suffix carries the prior denier group into the command
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah does not rename the audience; the bound suffix imports the already-known rejecters into the command.
topics.reason: The pronoun antecedent evidence supports a prior third-person group, matching the CRITICAL focus on continuity across the boundary.

topics.headline: away-from vector prepares toward-vector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah is built on opposing directions: away from them and toward the final destination.
topics.reason: Both prepositional relations are locally forced, so the vector contrast is a valid structural payoff.

words.gloss_range: accusative temporal adverb; locally opens the time frame for the caller and his summons
words.root_gloss_range: range from ordinary day to appointed period, epoch, event-day, and marked occasion; local use selects an eschatological time frame rather than ordinary daytime

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: call verb governed by the temporal frame

words.prose: {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) turns the ayah from the interpersonal command into the time-frame of the summons. Grammatically it is an accusative temporal adverb for the calling, while its placement also keeps the command and the scene adjacent: the withdrawal is followed by the Day when the caller calls. The word opens a frame that continues beyond this ayah into the emergence and speech of the next scene (54:7) and (54:8). Its root range allows more than ordinary daylight; here it feels like an appointed eschatological occasion, a decisive time-unit in which the earlier warning question is carried into judgment-time.

topics.headline: temporal pivot from command to call
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the time word is the hinge from direct command into the calling scene, with primary attachment to the call rather than a free-floating date.
topics.reason: The attachment evidence supports {{ar:يَوْمَ}} ({{tr:yawma}}) as the temporal frame of {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}); broader attachment ambiguity survives as adjacency, not as a competing parse that overrides it.

topics.headline: time frame continues into the next scene
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah opens a scene whose syntax and imagery continue into the following emergence and response (54:7) and (54:8).
topics.reason: The bundle explicitly recommends reading the temporal frame with the following scene, so the cross-ayah pressure is retained with concrete references.

topics.headline: ordinary day word becomes appointed event-time
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the familiar day-word is locally stretched into an appointed eschatological occasion rather than mere calendar time.
topics.reason: The root range licenses epoch and event-day pressure, while the local call scene narrows it to eschatological time.

words.gloss_range: third-person masculine singular imperfect call; locally an active summons directed by the following goal preposition
words.root_gloss_range: root field of calling, summoning, inviting, invoking, naming, and claim-making; local frame selects a summons toward a goal, with no expressed called audience

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: goal noun reached through the preposition
following caller subject from the same root

words.prose: {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}) animates the time-frame: the Day is defined by an ongoing act of calling. The imperfect form makes the summons feel active as the scene opens, and the following {{ar:إِلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ilā}}) directs it toward a goal rather than taking {{ar:شَىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shayʾin}}) as a direct object. The subject is then supplied overtly by {{ar:ٱلدَّاعِ}} ({{tr:al-dāʿi}}), so the root repeats as event and caller. The root family can include naming or claim-making, but here that pressure is narrowed: the call does not name the destination; it summons toward an unnamed, alien thing, handing failed warning speech over to the eschatological summons. The clipped written surface preserves the recited verb while making the call visually brief before the fuller caller title.

topics.headline: imperfect summons directed toward a goal
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the Day is not merely dated; it is animated by an active call moving toward a destination.
topics.reason: The verb instance marks an imperfect call with {{ar:إِلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ilā}}) and no direct object, matching the goal-directed summons topic.

topics.headline: verb anticipates and echoes the caller noun
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah concentrates the call by stating the action and then naming the caller from the same root.
topics.reason: The overt following subject is the active participle from the same root, so the event-caller echo is locally forced.

topics.headline: call-field pressure without naming the destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the irony that a root capable of naming or claim-making here summons toward what remains unnamed and unclassified.
topics.reason: The broader root senses are meaningful, but the local syntax supplies no named object and keeps the destination as a goal phrase.

topics.headline: brief written verb before fuller caller title
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the compact written verb before the expanded caller noun, while recitation and grammar still preserve the imperfect call.
topics.reason: The orthographic rows are retained as surface pressure, but the local grammar remains the imperfect verb rather than a new lexical sense.

words.gloss_range: definite active participle, the caller; locally the overt singular subject of the preceding call verb
words.root_gloss_range: root field of calling, summoning, inviting, invoking, and naming; local participle selects the agent identified by the act of calling

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: preceding call verb whose subject is the caller
final destination phrase contrasted with the definite caller

words.prose: {{ar:ٱلدَّاعِ}} ({{tr:al-dāʿi}}) resolves the action after the verb has already sounded: the call comes first, then the caller is named. The definite article and masculine singular agreement make this an identifiable subject of {{ar:يَدْعُ}} ({{tr:yadʿu}}), not a loose descriptive noun. As an active participle, it defines the agent by the act itself, like a herald or summoner whose role is to call. This makes the contrast sharper: the caller is grammatically definite and recognizable, while the destination remains {{ar:شَىْءٍ نُّكُرٍ}} ({{tr:shayʾin nukurin}}), an unrecognized thing. Same-root repetition with the verb, and the later same-surah reprise of rushing to the caller (54:8), keep the summons as the scene's organizing sound. Variant and phonetic rows affect closure weight, but they do not create a new referent.

topics.headline: definite delayed subject of the call
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the actor is withheld until after the call verb and then arrives as a definite singular subject.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces the participle as subject of the verb, and definiteness supports the identifiable-caller payoff.

topics.headline: agent defined by the calling act
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the noun is not just a name for a person; its participle form makes the role itself, the caller, carry the scene.
topics.reason: The active participle form and limited form group support treating the role-form as salient.

topics.headline: definite caller against unrecognizable destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a contrast between the definite caller and the unnamed alien destination, with the call-root repeated through the scene and into (54:8).
topics.reason: The same root appears in the verb and participle, and the bundle supplies same-surah call-chain pressure including (54:8).

topics.headline: variant and sound pressure without referent change
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant closure and sound shape can change the weight of the caller title while leaving the same subject relation intact.
topics.reason: The variant and phonetic rows survive as form pressure, but attachment evidence keeps the word as the same overt subject.

words.gloss_range: directional preposition; locally marks the goal of the call and governs the following genitive destination phrase

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: following genitive goal governed by the preposition
earlier away-from phrase contrasted with the toward-vector

words.prose: {{ar:إِلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ilā}}) turns the call into directed movement. It governs {{ar:شَىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shayʾin}}), making the final phrase the goal of the summons rather than a direct object or the called audience. This preposition also answers the earlier {{ar:عَنْهُمْ}} ({{tr:ʿanhum}}): the ayah first commands movement away from them, then stages a summons toward a thing. Its long final shape opens the delayed destination phrase before the heavier indefinite closure arrives.

topics.headline: goal of the call
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the call is goal-directed toward the final phrase, not object-taking in a way that would make the thing the called audience.
topics.reason: Attachment evidence forces the following noun as the governed goal complement of the call.

topics.headline: toward-vector answers away-from vector
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices the ayah's directional architecture: away from the deniers, toward the alien destination.
topics.reason: Both prepositional vectors are locally present and syntactically anchored.

topics.headline: preposition opens the delayed destination phrase
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the destination is delayed until this preposition opens the final phrase, giving the closure its approach-like movement.
topics.reason: The preposition stands before the final genitive phrase and governs it, preserving the structural and cadence rows.

words.gloss_range: indefinite genitive noun meaning a thing, matter, affair, or phenomenon; locally the unspecified goal of the call
words.root_gloss_range: broad designation for any thing, entity, affair, matter, or predicable reality; local use keeps maximal non-specification under the alien adjective

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: governing preposition that makes the noun a goal
following adjective that classifies the unspecified noun

words.prose: {{ar:شَىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shayʾin}}) is the goal reached through {{ar:إِلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ilā}}), not the direct object of the call. Its very generality is the point: after command, time frame, verb, caller, and preposition, the destination finally appears as the broadest kind of noun, singular and indefinite, refusing a familiar class label. Then {{ar:نُّكُرٍ}} ({{tr:nukurin}}) supplies the stark quality that the noun itself withholds. The result is not simply a strange object but an unclassified reality or event, with the noun and adjective bound by shared genitive indefiniteness and tanwin cadence. Same-surah uses of thing-language at (54:49) and (54:52) can be kept as a lexical thread, but here the local payoff is the withheld destination made alien by its adjective.

topics.headline: genitive goal, not direct object
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the thing is the endpoint toward which the call moves, not the audience being called or an object consumed by the verb.
topics.reason: The following noun is governed by {{ar:إِلَىٰ}} ({{tr:ilā}}), and the bundle explicitly flags the transfer risk.

topics.headline: maximally broad indefinite destination
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah withholds a specific name for the destination and uses the most general noun so the adjective must carry recognition-failure.
topics.reason: The local noun is singular indefinite and semantically broad, matching the CRITICAL rows about non-specification and unclassified reality.

topics.headline: noun and alien adjective close as a bound pair
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the final phrase works as a paired closure: an unnamed thing grammatically bound to its alien quality.
topics.reason: The adjective agreement and narrow co-occurrence support the construction-level payoff.

topics.headline: same-surah thing-language as lexical thread
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices a possible same-surah thread of thing-language at (54:49) and (54:52), while the local word remains governed by the call scene.
topics.reason: The recurrence is meaningful as a thread, but it does not override the local governed destination phrase.

words.gloss_range: indefinite genitive qualitative adjective meaning alien, unrecognizable, or intensely unfamiliar; locally modifies the unspecified thing
words.root_gloss_range: root field of non-recognition, denial, rejection, reprehensibility, and alienness; local adjective selects extreme unrecognizability with rejection-field pressure

supporting_anchors.gloss_range: noun modified by the final adjective
lighter adjective variant used as form contrast
passive variant used as syntax and meaning contrast

words.prose: {{ar:نُّكُرٍ}} ({{tr:nukurin}}) is the final adjective, not a new referent. Its genitive indefiniteness agrees with {{ar:شَىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shayʾin}}), so the alien quality belongs exactly to the thing toward which the call moves. The root {{ar:ن ك ر}} ({{tr:n-k-r}}) brings failure of recognition and rejection-field pressure; in this intensive adjective the destination becomes not merely strange but cognitively alien, outside familiar classification. Because it lands last, the ayah closes on unrecognizability rather than on the caller or the act of calling. Variant forms such as {{ar:نُكْرٍ}} ({{tr:nukrin}}) and {{ar:نُكِرَ}} ({{tr:nukira}}) expose lighter sound or passive rejection pressure, but the local canonical syntax keeps {{ar:نُّكُرٍ}} ({{tr:nukurin}}) as the adjective sealing the phrase.

topics.headline: final adjective locked to the thing
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the ayah ends by assigning alien quality to the unnamed destination, not by adding a separate event or actor.
topics.reason: The adjective agreement is locally forced, and final position makes the quality the closing weight.

topics.headline: intensive non-recognition and rejection pressure
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that the adjective is stronger than ordinary strangeness: it marks a destination that defeats recognition and carries rejection-field pressure.
topics.reason: The broader root family supports recognition and rejection pressure, while local adjective syntax narrows that pressure to qualitative alienness rather than a separate ethical claim.

topics.headline: variant sound and passive-rejection contrast
topics.reader_payoff: The reader notices that variant evidence tests whether the final element is heard as heavier adjective, lighter adjective, or passive denied event, while the local reading keeps the adjective.
topics.reason: Variant rows are useful as apparatus and contrast, but the local parse remains the agreeing adjective modifying {{ar:شَىْءٍ}} ({{tr:shayʾin}}).

baseline_models.mechanism: The verse pivots from commanded disengagement to a dated counter-motion: the messenger leaves their relational field, while a caller later bends attention and movement toward a destination.

activation_trace.role: Turning away and breaking proximity supplies the first, outward vector.
Calling that inclines by speech supplies the opposed, destination-directed vector.
A day as a descending severe event makes the pivot an event-phase rather than a calendar label.

changed_reading.before: Withdraw from them now; later a caller will issue a call.
changed_reading.after: The ayah stages a reversal of orientation: present disengagement clears the field for a future summons that reorients its hearers.

baseline_models.mechanism: The noun offers a thing that can be known and reported, but its adjective marks failed recognition and possible alteration into an unknown or unwelcome state. Indefiniteness does not erase the object; it foregrounds an encounter that defeats prior categories.

activation_trace.role: The general knowable and reportable thing preserves an object of encounter.
The contrary of recognition makes the encounter an epistemic failure.
Change into an unknown or disliked state adds transformation, not mere missing information.

changed_reading.before: The caller summons them to an unspecified dreadful thing.
changed_reading.after: The caller summons them into contact with something in principle knowable whose altered presentation defeats recognition.

context_deltas.mechanism: Approaching time, opened structure, and the settling of every matter turn the focus day into a terminal phase already advancing. The strange thing is encountered when an order that has split reaches fixation.

activation_trace.role: The day as a severe occurrence is the focus phase being temporally sharpened.
The severe, difficult, strange affair supplies the focus phase's felt quality.
Temporal nearness and exhaustion of an interval move the focus day from remote date to arriving boundary.
Splitting and opening supply the threshold image through which the terminal phase appears.
Matter as state or affair gives the process an ordered object.
Fixation and settlement make the approaching process culminative rather than chaotic.

structural_cues: 54:1 announces approach and rupture; 54:3 closes with every matter settling; 54:6 dates the call by 'day'.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies approach, splitting, and settlement; I infer a threshold-to-fixation sequence culminating in the focus call. A live alternative is that these are parallel signs without a causal sequence.

changed_reading.before: The call belongs to an unspecified future day.
changed_reading.after: The call is the operative threshold of an already approaching process in which ruptured order settles into an unavoidable affair.

context_deltas.mechanism: Their response to a visible sign is to turn a side away; the focus command then turns the messenger away from them. The same relational break returns with reversed agent and object, making withdrawal a measured closure of refused attention.

activation_trace.role: Deliberate turning away supplies the returned act, now assigned to the messenger.
Actual seeing establishes that their withdrawal follows perception rather than lack of access.
A manifest sign supplies the visible object from which they turn.
Turning the side away supplies the earlier human act mirrored by the focus imperative.

structural_cues: 54:2 sequences seeing a sign before their turning away; 54:6 begins with فَ and reverses who withdraws from whom.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies two lexically distinct acts of turning away; I infer reciprocal reversal and closure from their sequence and exchanged roles. They may alternatively be independent descriptions of rejection and prophetic disengagement.

changed_reading.before: The messenger is simply told to stop attending to them.
changed_reading.after: The messenger's withdrawal returns their sign-rejection to them, ending a relation they first broke despite seeing.

context_deltas.mechanism: Reports have carried vocal restraint, wisdom has reached its limit, and warnings fail to suffice. The focus withdrawal therefore closes admonitory speech; the next voice is not another attempt to caution but an effective summons to encounter.

activation_trace.role: Withdrawal marks the boundary between two speech regimes.
The later call inclines hearers toward a destination rather than merely advising them.
Vocal rebuke and restraint define the admonitory function that has already arrived.
Restraint for correction frames wisdom as attempted repair.
Reaching the limit presents that corrective communication as fully delivered.
Failure of sufficiency explains why further warning no longer changes the relation.
Warning meant to awaken caution names the speech act whose efficacy has failed.

structural_cues: 54:4-6 moves from restraining reports, to consummate wisdom, to warnings that do not avail, to withdrawal, and only then to the caller.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies completed warning and its insufficiency; I infer a functional regime change from persuasion to summons. A live alternative is that the future call remains itself another warning rather than execution.

changed_reading.before: The future caller continues the earlier warning activity.
changed_reading.after: The ayah closes warning as failed persuasion and announces a qualitatively different voice whose call effects encounter.

context_deltas.mechanism: The next scene gives the summons a body: people exit confinement, spread, then hurry toward the caller. This turns the focus opposition between 'away from them' and 'toward' into a mass spatial reversal, with the call functioning as a kinetic attractor.

activation_trace.role: The messenger's outward motion establishes one pole of the counter-motion.
Speech that inclines toward something establishes the attracting pole.
Passage into the outside makes response to the call bodily and spatial.
Opening, spreading, and branching turn released bodies into a field of motion.
Rapid forward approach supplies the velocity and direction of compliance.
The repeated caller resolves the focus call as the destination of the crowd's approach.
The event-day repeats the focus dating and identifies the motion's phase.
Difficulty and severity specify how the summoned encounter is experienced.

structural_cues: 54:6 has عَنْهُمْ then إِلَىٰ; 54:7-8 unfolds exit, dispersal, and rapid movement إِلَى ٱلدَّاعِ.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies the opposed prepositions and the following movement sequence; I infer that the call organizes a mass vector rather than only transmitting words. The live alternative is a plain chronological description with no designed counter-motion.

changed_reading.before: A caller verbally announces a dreadful destination.
changed_reading.after: The caller becomes the organizing center of involuntary collective motion, reversing the verse's initial withdrawal.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier messenger is denied and rebuked; once described as overpowered, he calls his sovereign for redress. Against that pattern, the focus's doubled caller-form marks a transfer from blocked human address to a call backed by effective agency.

activation_trace.role: The doubled verb and caller noun foreground calling as the mechanism whose efficacy is at issue.
Repeated attribution of falsehood supplies communicative blockage.
Vocal rebuke shows the messenger's address answered by counter-speech and restraint.
The messenger's call redirects speech toward the sovereign source of response.
Sovereignty and mastery supply the agency to which the defeated call is transferred.
Overpowering force marks the point at which ordinary address has reached defeat.
Vindication of the wronged gives the redirected call an effective answer.

structural_cues: 54:9-10 sequences denial, rebuke, confessed defeat, and a call for redress; 54:6 intensifies call by pairing verb and agent noun.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies blocked address, an upward redirection of calling, and requested redress; I infer a relay from ineffective warning to sovereignly effective summons. It may instead be only a recurring call motif with no transfer of agency.

changed_reading.before: The identity of the future caller alone gives the call authority.
changed_reading.after: The focus call carries the accumulated force of address transferred beyond defeated messengers and returned as an effective summons.

context_deltas.mechanism: The flood sequence repeatedly opens boundaries, releases flow, and brings separate waters to a measured meeting for an affair. Read analogically, the focus caller opens a channel through which separated hearers converge toward the 'thing'; the summons is a routing event, not merely information.

activation_trace.role: Calling that inclines toward a destination supplies the human-directional channel.
Being carried or compelled to an affair lets the destination function as an implemented outcome.
Opening a closure and widening ingress supplies the release condition.
An entrance supplies the bounded route through which release proceeds.
Appearance and abundance of water supply the moving material.
Pouring and downflow supply sustained movement after opening.
Wide rupture and eruption add a second released source.
Two opposed streams arriving together supply convergence.
Affair or state supplies the non-material outcome for which convergence occurs.
A measured limit makes convergence directed and bounded rather than accidental.

structural_cues: 54:11-12 sequences opening, pouring, eruption, meeting, and a measured affair; 54:6 directs a call إِلَىٰ a thing.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a concrete release-and-convergence mechanism; I map its directional logic, not its water substance, onto the focus syntax. The materially live alternative is that the flood episode offers no analogy for the caller.

changed_reading.before: The call names a destination for independent respondents.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the call opens and routes a convergence whose destination is an already measured affair.

context_deltas.mechanism: A manifest sign is left as a surviving trace and recitation is made easy for recollection. The focus's unrecognizable thing is therefore not hidden by lack of disclosure; it is the endpoint of a failed capacity or refusal to recognize what signs and reminders kept available.

activation_trace.role: A knowable and reportable thing keeps the destination available to cognition.
Non-recognition locates the crisis in acknowledgment rather than simple invisibility.
Alteration into an unwelcome state explains why disclosed reality is encountered as alien.
Leaving an enduring trace supplies persistence of evidence.
A manifest sign defines that trace as publicly legible.
A reminder that causes recollection states the trace's intended cognitive function.
Ease after difficulty removes inaccessibility as the main explanation for non-recognition.
Recitation supplies the repeatable medium of disclosure.
Restoring something from forgetting supplies the recognition that remains possible but unrealized.

structural_cues: 54:15 asks about remembering after a sign was left; 54:17 repeats the invitation to remember after declaring the recitation easy.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies preserved sign, accessible recitation, and repeated recollection; I infer that focus non-recognition indicts the receiver rather than the availability of evidence. The adjective can still denote objective severity independent of any epistemic failure.

changed_reading.before: The destination is alien because it was unspecified or undisclosed.
changed_reading.after: The destination is encountered as alien despite sustained disclosure, exposing a breakdown of recognition rather than an absence of signs.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it activates the split mapped root د ع ع beneath the surface root د ع و and joins speech to severe pushing. It remains anchored in the doubled focus call, the following rush toward the caller, and the later image of forceful driving; downstream prose should say the summons acts 'as if' propulsion, not claim that the focus verb literally means shove.

activation_trace.role: Severe pushing supplies an exploratory force-image beneath the doubled call.
Being carried or compelled to an affair gives the force a focus-anchored destination.
Rapid forward approach makes the summons visibly effective as motion.
Forceful driving supplies a contained material analogy for effective propulsion.

changed_reading.before: The caller communicates and the hearers subsequently move.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, the call itself operates like a driving force that compels movement into the appointed affair.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because singular 'thing' is read through the following collective body's changed surface rather than as a detached event. It remains anchored in the focus branches of disfigured form and transformation into the unrecognized, then gains visible mechanism from grave-exit, exposure, and spreading; downstream prose should present it as a possible spectacle or process, not identify the grammatical referent with certainty.

activation_trace.role: Altered or disfigured form lets the generic thing denote a startling presented configuration.
Change into an unknown or unwelcome state makes reconfiguration the cause of non-recognition.
The grave supplies the prior enclosure from which the collective form emerges.
A form departing from its familiar type sharpens the exploratory transformation mechanism.
Exposure by stripping a covering makes the emergent scene newly visible.
Opening and branching spread the reconfigured collective across the visual field.

changed_reading.before: The 'unrecognized thing' is an external event awaiting the crowd.
changed_reading.after: Exploratorily, it can include the crowd's own reconfigured emergence as an alien spectacle and process.

strongest_changes: The messenger's withdrawal mirrors and returns the audience's earlier sign-rejection.
Failed warning gives way to an effective summons that organizes bodily counter-motion toward the caller.
The unknown thing becomes a crisis of recognition despite preserved signs and accessible reminder.
The Noah sequence supports a contained model of calling transferred from defeated address to effective agency.
summary.what_was_special: The focus ayah is a hinge of vectors and speech regimes: away from them becomes movement toward the caller, warning becomes summons, and a knowable thing becomes unrecognizable at encounter. The packet's split root inventory also preserves a cautious propulsion reading that a conservative synthesis would likely lose.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether شَىْءٍ نُّكُرٍ points primarily to an object, an event, a condition, or the crowd's own transformed spectacle remains open.
The د ع ع propulsion activation is branch-distant and should remain analogical.
The flood-channel model depends on transferring directional structure across domains rather than on a direct lexical equation.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **A reversal of orientation links withdrawal to compulsory approach.** `و ل ي` B007 is turning away and withdrawal, while `د ع و` B001 is calling to draw near. The imperative withdrawal now is followed by a day when caller and calling are doubled. The packet supplies the opposed motions; I infer that refused proximity in the present is reversed into unavoidable response later. The ayah reads as a spatial-temporal hinge: leave them, until they must move toward the call.

2. **The called object remains both unrecognized and severe.** `ن ك ر` B001 is the contrary of recognition, B003 the severe and unfamiliar thing, and B006 the condemned thing that prompts correction. The indefinite `شَىْءٍ` (`ش ي ء` B001, knowable thing) is paradoxically qualified as not recognized. I infer that the call reveals a reality whose knowability does not make it familiar or welcome. The object can remain strange, terrible, and morally repudiating without being prematurely specified.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: Later 54:44–45 supplies another orientation reversal: the gathered claim to prevail becomes backs turned in flight. Together with 54:48’s face-first dragging, it makes the present opposition between voluntary withdrawal and compelled movement part of a larger body-direction mechanism.

reader_a.activated_readings_md:
1. **`و ل ي / B007` (turning away and withdrawal).** The imperative answers the audience's `يُعْرِضُوا` in 54:2 with a controlled reversal of orientation. Their side-turn is answered by the messenger's withdrawal, after which a caller they cannot evade takes over. The packet supplies the two turnings and later summons; I infer voluntary refusal -> withdrawal of address -> compulsory call. **Reading change:** `فَتَوَلَّ عَنْهُم` marks a transfer of agency, not simple abandonment.
2. **`د ع و / B001` (calling to draw near by voice or speech).** Verb and agent repeat the root (`يَدْعُ ٱلدَّاعِ`), and 54:7-8 supplies the resulting emergence and hurry. The call's assigned role is a vector that pulls a dispersed population toward one destination. The packet states call then motion; I infer call -> draws and aligns that motion. **Reading change:** the caller does not merely announce an event; the call organizes bodies.
3. **`ن ك ر / B004` (change into an unrecognized or disliked state), alongside `B003` (the severe unfamiliar thing).** Graves opening in 54:7 and the sky opening in 54:11 make alteration of the known order more salient than mere novelty. The packet supplies the unfamiliar destination and nearby reversals of enclosure; I infer altered order -> produces nonrecognition. **Reading change:** `شَيْءٍ نُكُرٍ` can be the world made unrecognizable, not only an unknown object within an unchanged world.
reader_a.retrospective_surprises_md: 54:7-8 confirmed that the doubled call organizes gaze, neck, and speed; 54:11 then made نكر describe an altered order whose sky-boundary opens.

identity_judgment.rationale: Kaynak ifadesi iki bağlı süreci açıkça verir: duvarların birbiri ardından çökmesi ve yapıların birbiri ardından yıkılması. Hazırlanan çerçeve, ardışıklığı ve çökme ile ettirgen yıkma ayrımını korur.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi, tökezleyen kişiye yöneltilen ikili bir sözün ayağa kalkma ve toparlanma işlevini açıkça verir. Bu, genel bir itme ya da genel bir teselli değil, belirli durumda kullanılan sözlü bir teşviktir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Anlam tökezleyen muhataba söylenen kalıpla sınırlıdır; genel ayağa kalkma, yardım etme veya teselli etme anlamına genişletilmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Dal yalnızca tökezleyen kişiye yöneltilen özel sözlü kalıbı açıklar; bundan çıplak bir kök anlamı çıkarılmaz.

concept_gloss.applicability: Belirli sözün tökezleyen kişiye yöneltilen teşvik işlevini eksiksiz karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Ayağa kalkma buyruğunu ve toparlanma teşvikini doğal Türkçeyle korur.

error_profile.loses: Ayağa kalkma ve hemen toparlanma çağrısını kaybeder.
error_profile.adds: Hastalık veya yaralanma sonrasında kullanılan genel dileği ekler.
error_profile.collision: Türkçedeki hastalık ve kaza sonrası nezaket kalıbıyla karışır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın kurucu yönü ayağa kalkma ve toparlanma çağrısıdır; komşu dal daha geniş bir durumda koruyucu esenlik dileği olarak kullanılabilir.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi koşuyu iki eşzamanlı özellikle sınırlar: hareket doğrusal değil kıvrımlı veya dolambaçlıdır ve hızlı değil yavaştır. Dalın ayırıcı kimliği yalnızca koşma değil, bu özel hareket biçimidir.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Yavaşlık ve kıvrımlı ilerleyiş birlikte kurucudur; sıradan koşu, ağır yürüyüş veya yorgunluktan sendeleme bu dala girmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Tanım çıplak dalın kıvrımlı ve yavaş koşma anlamıyla sınırlıdır; komşu hareket biçimleri veya özel yapılar eklenmez.

facets.statement: Hareket yürüyüş değil koşudur ve ilerleme görece yavaştır.
Koşunun yolu ya da beden hareketi kıvrımlı ve dolambaçlıdır.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarımlar, koşunun kıvrımlı ilerleyişini ve yavaş temposunu birlikte kurucu özellikler olarak verir.

concept_gloss.applicability: Dalın hem hareket türünü hem hızını hem de izlediği biçimi birlikte karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Koşmayı, yavaşlığı ve kıvrımlı ilerleyişi eksiksiz korur.

error_profile.loses: Koşunun görece yavaş temposunu açıkça belirtmez.

error_profile.collision: Yavaş ve ölçülü yürüme anlamıyla karışır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal yavaş ve kıvrımlı koşmayı bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal çok hızlı, güçlü ve doğrultusunda süren koşuyu bildirir.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: yavaş kıvrımlı koşu ile hızlı koşu

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Ortak eksen koşunun hızı ve seyir biçimidir; odak dal yavaş ve dolambaçlı, komşu dal hızlı ve güçlü ilerleyişi öne çıkarır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal kıvrımlı bir koşma biçimidir.

neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki dal yavaş ilerleme izlenimi verir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Hız benzerliği yanıltıcıdır: odak dal yine koşudur ve kıvrımlıdır; komşu dal ise koşma içermeyen temkinli yürüyüştür.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi sözcüğü kısa boylu adam için açıklar, fakat biçimin doğruluğunu koşullu verir ve başka bir biçimden ses değişimiyle gelmiş olabileceğini belirtir. Anlam korunabilir, ancak bağımsız ve üretken bir kök anlamı olduğu varsayılamaz.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal kısa boylu erkek kişiyi adlandırır; biçimin kökeni ve bağımsızlığı belirsiz olduğu için genel kısalık anlamına genişletilmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Kabul edilmiş sözcük birimi bulunmadığından dalın çıplak veya yapıya bağlı olduğu varsayılmaz; tanım yalnızca aktarılan kişi niteliğini kaydeder.

concept_map.definition: Kısa boylu bir erkeği niteleyen, biçimsel doğruluğu ve başka bir sözcükten ses değişimiyle gelip gelmediği belirsiz bir adlandırmadır.

facets.statement: Adlandırmanın gönderimi kısa boylu erkek kişidir.
Biçimin başka bir kısa-boy adlandırmasından ses değişimiyle gelmiş olması mümkündür.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Aktarımlar kısa boylu erkek anlamını desteklerken biçimin bağımsızlığı konusunda ihtiyat kaydı taşır.

concept_gloss.applicability: Belirsiz köken kaydını anlamın içine katmadan aktarılan kişi niteliğini karşılar.

error_profile.preserves: Erkek kişi gönderimini ve kısa boy niteliğini tam olarak korur.

contextual_glosses.applicability: Nadir adlandırmanın açıklayıcı ve doğal Türkçe karşılığı gerektiğinde kullanılır.

error_profile.preserves: Kişinin cinsiyetini ve boyca kısa oluşunu doğrudan korur.
Boyca kısa olma niteliğini korur.
error_profile.adds: İnsan dışındaki bitki ve nesnelere, ayrıca tıknazlığa uzanan kapsam ekler.
error_profile.collision: Türkçede kısa boy yanında gövdece sıkı veya gelişmemiş olma çağrışımı taşır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal kısa boylu erkek için özel ve kökeni belirsiz bir adlandırmadır.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal kişi ve cisimlerde kısalığı genel bir nitelik olarak kapsar.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: özel kısa-adam adı ile genel kısalık
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: İki dal da bir insanın boyca kısa oluşunu ifade edebilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dalın gönderimi erkek kişiyle ve belirli bir adlandırmayla sınırlıdır; komşu dal ise kısalık niteliğini daha geniş varlık sınıflarında anlatır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal yalnızca kısa boylu erkek gönderimini verir.
neighbor_distinctions.neighbor_only: Komşu dal kısa olmanın yanında bedenin toplu ve yaratılışça kısalmış görünmesini içerir.
neighbor_distinctions.gloss: kısa adam ile kısa ve toplu yapı
neighbor_distinctions.shared_zone: Her iki adlandırma kısa boylu bir erkeğe uygulanabilir.
neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Odak dal için kısa boy yeterlidir; komşu dalın sınırında toplu beden yapısı ve boyun kesilmiş gibi oluşuna ilişkin ek bir tasarım vardır.

identity_judgment.rationale: Yetkili kaynak ifadesi iki yakın görünümü birlikte aktarır: iki hurma ağacı arasındaki açıklık ve seyrek duran hurma ağaçları. Ayrıca sözcüğün ilk ünsüzünün başka bir biçimde aktarılmış olabileceği belirtilir; bu nedenle dal hem yerleşim anlamını hem yazım belirsizliğini korumalıdır.
identity_judgment.boundary_note: Dal hurmaların seyrekliği veya iki hurma arasındaki açıklıkla sınırlıdır; küçük hurma, toplu hurmalık ya da genel ağaçlık anlamına gelmez.

lexicalization_scope.note: Kabul edilmiş sözcük birimi bulunmadığından çıplaklık varsayılmaz; yalnızca seyrek hurmalar ve aralarındaki açıklık aktarılır.

concept_map.definition: Seyrek duran hurma ağaçlarını veya iki hurma ağacı arasında kalan açıklığı anlatan, ilk ünsüzü konusunda aktarım ayrılığı bulunan bir adlandırmadır.

facets.statement: Hurma ağaçları bitişik bir topluluk değil, aralıklı ve seyrek durumdadır.
Adlandırma iki hurma ağacı arasında kalan boşluğa da uygulanır.
Sözcüğün ilk ünsüzü başka bir sesle aktarılmış bir biçime ait olabilir.

source_synthesis.common_summary: Tek aktarım seyrek hurmalar ile iki hurma arasındaki açıklığı aynı adlandırmada birleştirir ve biçim için bir ses varyantı kaydeder.

source_details.summary: Seyrek hurmalar, aralarındaki açıklık ve olası ses varyantı bu tek tanıklıkta birlikte korunur.

concept_gloss.text: iki hurma arasındaki açıklık veya seyrek hurmalar

error_profile.adds: Sık veya düzenli dikilmiş her türlü hurma bahçesini kapsar.
error_profile.collision: Toplu ve düzenli hurma bahçesi anlamıyla karışır.

neighbor_distinctions.distinction: Ortak düzen ekseninde odak dal aralık ve dağınıklığı, komşu dal ise ağaçların bir araya gelerek topluluk oluşturmasını öne çıkarır.

neighbor_distinctions.focus_only: Odak dal ağaçların birbirine göre seyrek yerleşimini bildirir.

Bazı dallar tanınmış olandan uzaklaşma düşüncesiyle bağlanırken bazıları bağımsızlaşmış somut veya karşılıklı eylem alanlarıdır.

word_morpheme_spans.note: Accepted bridge links preserve independent analysis identities. Several analysis entries may share canonical morphemes. Read their distinct semantic claims; shared morphology alone is not duplication. Legacy aligned_qac_word_ref values are source observations, not QAC joins. Excluded source entries remain available with their explicit qualification.

word_analysis_qac_alignment.note: Legacy analysis and QAC numbers are separate source namespaces. Use accepted word_morpheme_spans for actual many-to-many joins. The legacy numbering observation is preserved, not used for alignment.

channel_review.note: first-pass blind review by a single reader; no adjudication, no accept/reject, no per-ayah channel maturity. Not a channel ledger.

channel_generated_outputs.note: Generated network-v3 channel discovery/family/path outputs are available as external quran-data files; read them only when channel detail is necessary, and do not treat them as an adjudicated channel ledger.

missing_branch_inventories.reason: no accepted, non-contaminated branch inventory in resource

full_context_packet.note: surah-scope fallback: the default commentary workflow does not consume per-ayah focus packets, so the source packet is scoped by this builder to roots this ayah can justify and carries no staged reveal order

scoping.note: SCOPED, NOT ABSENT. The surah-scope fallback inventory covers every root in the surah; it is narrowed here to roots this ayah can justify -- roots occurring in this ayah (all their branches kept, unconditionally, because Layer 2 selects nothing) plus roots explicitly cited by channel material anchored here (only the cited branches kept, enough to resolve the citation). A root listed in dropped_roots is a deliberate scoping decision, not a missing source.

v12_reader_responses.note: Per-ayah focus-run reader responses are retired from the default commentary workflow. Use regular reader walks, plus/minus-5 reader walks, and cross-run publication findings for corpus-wide reader-derived evidence.

v12_cross_run_publication.note: Compact final cross-run findings for this ayah, reconciled upstream from regular and plus/minus-5 reader runs; use as a coverage/priority check, not as replacement prose.

occurrence_evidence_trim.note: TRIMMED, NOT ABSENT. dictionary_entry.occurrence_evidence.occurrences and .ayahs are removed from every root by design: they are a per-occurrence QAC concordance and character-span alignment table carrying zero readings, branches or senses, and they dominated bundle size (~1.5 MB for a single common root). occurrence_evidence.summary (corpus frequency) and .forms (inflectional inventory) are retained. Dictionary/gloss branches are kept in full for every included Furuq root target.

branch_policy.note: No branch filtering is applied. Every branch present in each included dictionary/gloss root entry is kept.

root_mapping.policy: Use the dominant Furuq root for every QAC root, and include non-dominant Furuq targets as additional root_lexicon entries when qac-furuq-v4-root-map marks the QAC root as split.
